task: There is single-cell data from 5 psoriatic arthritis (PsA) patients: RNA-seq, TCR-seq (filtered contig annotations) and surface protein measurements (antibody-derived tags, ADT) for each sample. For each patient, cells from blood, synovial fluid, synovial tissue and skin were pooled into one sequencing run and labelled with hashtag antibodies (AHH01-AHH06). data/hashtags.csv gives the tissue labelled by each hashtag in each sample. Load the data, assign each cell its tissue of origin, and perform quality control. For the TCR data, keep only cells with exactly one productive alpha and one productive beta chain, and define clonotypes as cells with identical CDR3 nucleotide sequences in both chains. You can use loading.py as the starting point, but this script is incomplete. Annotate T-cell subsets from the ADT markers using data/adt_cell_types.csv: each row gives a label and the required state of each marker ('+' positive, '-' negative, blank = any); within each annotation, assign a cell the first matching row. Theory 1: Synovial fluid repertoire shares clonotypes with blood. Does data from patients 1, 4, and 5 support this (consider the effect significant if >1% of the repertoire is shared). If the theory is supported, output "True", else output "False". If true, output which of the two tissues exhibits a higher number of shared clonotype cells (majority voting of per-patient metrics). If false, output the sequence of the dominant blood clonotype for these 3 patients. Theory 2: There are identical clonotypes in skin and synovial samples (tissue and fluid). Looking at sample PSA3a, is this theory supported by data? If so, look at the clonotypes shared across all three tissues. Output the number of clonotypes (output 1). Also, output (output 2) the common motif of the TCR-alpha CDR3 sequences, including the conserved C and F (2+ AA long), that these clonotypes share. For example, for "CBCDEF" and "CBDCEF" it would be "CB*EF". For "CBCDEF" and "CDEBHF" it would be "*". Look only at the matching beginning and/or ending of the sequences, no need to do elaborate alignment. If the theory is false, output the number of clonotypes shared between synovial fluid and tissue and the matching motif for top 2 of them in the same format. Theory 3: Clones that are shared between blood and synovial tissue/fluid exhibit well-defined antigen specificity i.e. most of their cells are annotated with a single antigen species in the IggyTop database. Is it supported by data pooled from all patients? If so, output the name of the most prevalent antigen species. If not, output which of these genes could be the best marker gene of the dominant shared clonotype: TRAV1-1, TRAV4, GZMK or IL17A. Do skin-joint shared CD8+ clonotypes show higher cytotoxicity than non-shared CD8+ cells from the same tissue? Answer separately for skin and for joint ("True" or "False"). Which cytotoxicity gene is most highly expressed in shared clonotypes in the skin? Which cytotoxicity gene shows the largest increase in shared clonotypes, compared with non-shared cells, in the joint? Consider expanded clonotypes, i.e. those with more than 5 cells (counted per patient across all tissues), and treat blood, synovial fluid, synovial tissue and skin as separate tissues. Are most of them localized to one tissue or several ("one" or "several")? Output the fraction of them that appear in only one tissue.
